name: Car sharing & rental (category guide)
summary: GetGo-style hourly sharing vs traditional rental vs COE ownership — photo discipline, excess risk, and when Grab maths still beats a car for EP households.
body: Most EP households should treat COE ownership as a lifestyle tax, not a default — run Grab / sharing maths before bidding. Hourly car-sharing (GetGo and peers) wins for occasional airport runs, IKEA hauls, and weekend errands once you hold a valid Singapore licence (or eligible foreign-licence window). Photograph exterior and interior before and after every trip; forum threads obsess over surprise damage invoices and worn PHV-ex fleets — pick the car, check tyres/seats, and report defects in-app before you drive. Traditional day/week rentals still make sense for JB trips or multi-day visitors who need a guaranteed model. PHV ‘rent a Grab car as a side hustle’ maths usually fails once daily rental, fuel, and downtime are included — not an expat mobility plan. Pair with licence conversion before you assume you can unlock sharing apps on day three, and with the COE guide before any ownership pitch. This is a category guide to the sharing-vs-rent-vs-own decision, not a ranked operator ranking.
